Subject: FinLytics POC: success criteria, timeline and owners

Hi Sara / David,

Thanks again for taking the time today — great call. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we keep momentum going for the POC: 

Proposed POC scope (2 weeks):
- Ingest a representative dataset (up to 100k rows) from FinLytics into a sandbox instance.
- Run 3 common workflows: report summarization, anomaly detection prompts, and embedding-based search.
- Measure latency, cost/QPS, and qualitative output alignment on a 20-prompt eval set.

Draft success criteria (please confirm or update):
1) Average 95th percentile latency < 350ms for single-turn summarization on test payloads.
2) Embedding recall >= 0.85 on the eval set.
3) End-user quality score (scale 1-5) >= 4 on 15 manual checks.
4) Infrastructure fit: POC throughput >= 5 rps with under 20% CPU/GPU saturated for expected load.

Owners we need from your side:
- Technical lead (for data access & infra)
- Product owner (for quality acceptance)
- Security contact (for quick checklist / SOC2 questions)

From our side:
- Marissa (sales) – overall program owner, timeline and contract.
- Marcus Lin (eng) – POC engineer, integration & telemetry.
- Monica Patel (CS) – evaluation plan & quality checks.

Attachments: I attached a one-page mutual action plan and a short POC checklist to this thread (FinLytics_Mutual_Action_Plan_v1.xlsx, redwood-poc-checklist.pdf).

Proposed timeline:
- Week 0 (this week): Align success criteria, confirm owners, share data access method.
- Week 1: Data ingest and integration, basic flows working.
- Week 2: Run eval set, measure metrics, wrap up and decision meeting.

Can you confirm the success criteria above and share the technical lead who will own data access? If June 8 kickoff works, we’ll schedule a 30–45m technical kickoff.

Thanks,

Marissa Cole

Hi David — thanks for flagging. Short answers:
- We support private endpoints via AWS PrivateLink for dedicated/private deployments, and IP allowlist for hosted endpoints. For the sandbox POC we can provision an IP-restricted endpoint or a temporary PrivateLink connection — whichever fits your security team.
- Payload guidance: keep individual prompt payloads under 2,000 tokens for best latency; for long reports we recommend chunking by section with a context window of ~1,000 tokens and post-aggregation.

I’ll include a short runbook and the sandbox connection details in the Drive once you share the access method. If PrivateLink is preferred, put Priya Shah on the thread and we’ll coordinate.

—Marcus
